speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or a specific injury to that area? When did these symptoms first start, and are they constant or do they come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Based on the mechanism of injury (jersey pull) and the rapid onset of swelling and pain in the right ring finger, did you notice a sudden "pop" or snapping sensation at the moment of injury, and do you currently feel instability when you try to bend or straighten that finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Tendon Rupture of the Distal Phalanx)

The inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint, combined with the finger resting in extension and pain at that specific joint, confirms a disruption of the flexor mechanism or, more likely given the injury pattern, an associated flexor tenosynovitis or rupture. However, the classic "jersey finger" mechanism (pulling away forcefully) causing inability to *flex* the DIP joint is the specific injury I am looking for. I need to confirm if you can actively extend your finger against gravity, as this would rule out an extensor injury. Please also confirm if you can make a full fist with your other fingers.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
